storyTitle: The Eternal Bond of Savitri and Satyavan
description: A tale of eternal love that conquered even death itself
contentEnglish:
In the ancient kingdom of Madra, there lived Princess Savitri, whose beauty was matched only by her wisdom and devotion. When the time came for her to choose a husband, she traveled far and wide across the lands, seeking a companion worthy of her heart.

In a remote forest hermitage, she encountered Satyavan, the exiled prince living in simple dignity with his blind father. Though he wore bark clothes and lived humbly, his noble character shone like the sun. Savitri's heart recognized its eternal companion, and she declared her choice before the royal court.

The sage Narada warned King Ashwapati of a terrible prophecy: Satyavan was destined to die within a year. But Savitri's resolve remained unshaken. "A true heart chooses only once," she declared. "Whether his life be long or short, Satyavan alone shall be my husband."

Their wedding was simple but filled with profound joy. Savitri embraced the forest life with grace, serving her husband and blind father-in-law with unwavering devotion. Every moment with Satyavan deepened their bond, each shared glance and gentle word weaving their souls more tightly together.

As the fated day approached, Savitri accompanied Satyavan to gather wood. When he suddenly collapsed, she cradled him tenderly, watching helplessly as Yama, the God of Death, appeared to claim his soul. But love had given Savitri courage beyond mortal bounds. She followed Yama himself, her devotion so pure that even Death was moved.

Through her wisdom and unwavering love, Savitri won back her husband's life, proving that true love transcends even the boundary between life and death. Their reunion was sweeter than the first meeting, for they had conquered the ultimate separation. Thus, Savitri and Satyavan became immortal symbols of love's triumph over destiny itself.
contentSanskrit:
मद्रदेशे अश्वपतिः नाम राजा आसीत्। तस्य सावित्री नाम पुत्री आसीत् या रूपेण, बुद्ध्या च सर्वेषां मध्ये प्रसिद्धा आसीत्।

विवाहस्य समये सा देशान् भ्रमित्वा वनाश्रमे सत्यवान्तं नाम युवकं दृष्टवती। सः निर्वासितः राजपुत्रः आसीत् यः अन्धेन पित्रा सह वने वसति स्म। यद्यपि सः साधारणं जीवनं यापयति स्म, तथापि तस्य चरित्रं सूर्यवत् प्रकाशते स्म।

नारदऋषिः राजानं चेतयामास - "सत्यवान् एकस्मिन् वर्षे मरिष्यति।" परन्तु सावित्री निश्चयेन अवदत् - "सत्यहृदयं एकवारमेव वृणोति। सत्यवान् एव मम पतिः भविष्यति।"

तयोः विवाहः सरलः आसीत् परन्तु प्रेमपूर्णः। सावित्री पतिसेवायां तत्परा अभवत्। प्रत्येकं क्षणं तयोः बन्धनं दृढतरं भवति स्म।

निर्धारितदिने सत्यवान् कष्टं प्राप्य पतितः। यमराजः आगत्य तस्य प्राणान् नेतुम् ऐच्छत्। सावित्री प्रेमेण यमस्य अनुगमनं कृतवती। तस्याः भक्त्या यमः प्रसन्नः अभवत्।

सावित्री ज्ञानेन प्रेम्णा च सत्यवानस्य जीवनं पुनः प्राप्नोत्। इत्थं सा प्रमाणं कृतवती यत् सत्यप्रेमः मृत्युमपि जयति। सावित्री-सत्यवानौ प्रेमस्य शाश्वतं प्रतीकं अभवताम्।

storyTitle: The Witty Replies of Tenali Ramakrishna
description: Clever tales that bring joy through wit and wisdom
contentEnglish:
In the magnificent court of King Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara, there lived the legendary court jester Tenali Ramakrishna, whose wit was sharper than the finest sword and whose humor could dissolve the gravest of situations.

One day, a proud scholar arrived at court, boasting that he had mastered all languages and could defeat anyone in debate. The king, intrigued, summoned Tenali. The scholar sneered, "I speak twelve languages fluently. How many do you speak, jester?"

Tenali smiled humbly. "Only half a language, learned sir." The court erupted in laughter, and the scholar smirked triumphantly. But Tenali continued, "However, I have observed that you use twelve languages yet say nothing of value, while I use half a language and manage to communicate everything necessary. Perhaps quality matters more than quantity?"

The king laughed heartily, and even the scholar had to acknowledge the clever truth in Tenali's words. Another time, a miserly courtier bragged about his new mansion with a hundred rooms. Tenali congratulated him, then asked innocently, "But sir, forgive my simple mind—when you sleep at night, how many rooms can you use at once?"

The courtier stammered, "Well, only one, of course." Tenali nodded sagely. "How wonderful! Then you and I are equals in that regard. I too have one room for sleeping. It seems our true wealth is the same when night falls!"

Through such encounters, Tenali taught profound lessons wrapped in laughter—that wisdom often wears the garb of humor, that pride deserves gentle deflation, and that the greatest truths are best delivered with a smile. His wit became immortal, reminding us that intelligence combined with humor is a powerful force for good.
contentSanskrit:
विजयनगरस्य राज्ञः कृष्णदेवरायस्य सभायां तेनालीरामकृष्णः प्रसिद्धः विदूषकः आसीत् यस्य बुद्धिः सर्वेभ्यः तीक्ष्णतरा आसीत्।

एकदा गर्वितः पण्डितः आगत्य अवदत् - "अहं द्वादशभाषाः जानामि। त्वं कति भाषाः जानासि, विदूषक?" तेनालीः नम्रतया अवदत् - "अहं केवलं अर्धभाषां जानामि।"

सभा हसिता। परन्तु तेनालीः पुनः अवदत् - "भवान् द्वादशभाषाभिः किमपि मूल्यवत् न वदति, अहं तु अर्धभाषया सर्वं आवश्यकं कथयामि। गुणवत्ता परिमाणात् महत्त्वपूर्णा?"

राजा सहसा हसितवान्। पण्डितः तेनालेः बुद्धिं स्वीकृतवान्। अन्यस्मिन् अवसरे कृपणः सभासदः नूतनगृहस्य शतकक्षाणां विषये गर्वेण अकथयत्। तेनालीः अपृच्छत् - "रात्रौ निद्राकाले भवान् कति कक्षान् एकसमये उपयुङ्क्ते?"

सभासदः अवदत् - "एकं केवलं।" तेनालीः अवदत् - "अद्भुतम्! तदा वयं समानौ स्वः। मम अपि निद्रार्थं एकं कक्षं अस्ति। रात्रौ आवयोः सम्पत्तिः समाना भवति!"

एवं तेनालीः हास्येन महान्तं ज्ञानं शिक्षयति स्म - बुद्धिः हास्येन संयुक्ता महत्त्वपूर्णा भवति इति।

description: A moving story of compassion that transcends all boundaries
contentEnglish:
King Shibi was renowned throughout the three worlds for his unwavering commitment to dharma and his boundless compassion for all living beings. His fame reached even the celestial realms, where Indra and Agni decided to test the depth of his virtue.

One day, as Shibi held court, a terrified dove flew into the hall and took refuge in the king's lap, trembling with fear. Close behind came a fierce hawk, demanding its rightful prey. "O King," the hawk cried, "this dove is my food, destined by nature. Do not deny me what is mine!"

The dove pleaded with tear-filled eyes, "Great king, you are the protector of all who seek shelter. I have come to you in my hour of desperation. Please, save my life!" Shibi's heart was torn. How could he deny protection to one who sought refuge? Yet how could he let the hawk starve?

After deep contemplation, Shibi spoke with gentle resolve: "Noble hawk, I cannot surrender this soul who has sought my protection. But neither shall you go hungry. I offer you flesh from my own body, equal in weight to the dove." The court gasped in shock, but the king remained calm.

A scale was brought forth. Shibi placed the dove on one side and began cutting flesh from his thigh to place on the other. But mysteriously, the scale did not balance. He added more and more flesh from his body, yet still the dove weighed heavier. Finally, with a serene smile, the king himself sat upon the scale, offering his entire being.

At that moment, the hawk and dove revealed their true forms—Indra and Agni, the celestial beings. "Your compassion knows no bounds, O King," they proclaimed. "You have proven that true dharma transcends self-preservation." They blessed Shibi with immortal fame, and his story became a eternal reminder that compassion, when pure and complete, requires the surrender of the self for the sake of all beings.
contentSanskrit:
राजा शिबिः धर्मपरायणः करुणापूर्णः च आसीत्। तस्य कीर्तिः त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रसिद्धा आसीत्। इन्द्रः अग्निश्च तस्य परीक्षां कर्तुम् ऐच्छताम्।

एकदा भीता कपोतिका राजसभां प्रविश्य राज्ञः अङ्के आश्रयं प्राप्नोत्। तस्याः पृष्ठात् श्येनः आगत्य अवदत् - "राजन्, एषा मम आहारः। प्रकृत्या निर्धारितम् एतत्। मां मा वञ्चय!"

कपोतिका अश्रुपूर्णनेत्राभ्यां प्रार्थयत् - "महाराज, भवान् शरणागतानां रक्षकः। मम जीवनं रक्षतु!" शिबेः हृदयं विदीर्णम् अभवत्। किं करणीयम्?

गम्भीरं चिन्तयित्वा शिबिः अवदत् - "श्येन, अहं शरणागतां न समर्पयामि। परन्तु त्वम् अपि क्षुधार्तः न भविष्यसि। कपोत्याः तुल्यं मांसं मम शरीरात् गृहाण।"

तुला आनीता। एकस्मिन् पार्श्वे कपोतिका, अन्यस्मिन् राज्ञः मांसं स्थापितम्। परन्तु तुला न समतुला अभवत्। राजा अधिकाधिकं मांसं दत्तवान्, तथापि कपोतिका गुरुतरा आसीत्। अन्ते राजा स्वयमेव तुलायां उपविष्टः।

तदा श्येनः कपोतिका च स्वरूपं प्रकाशयाम् आसतुः - तौ इन्द्रः अग्निश्च आस्ताम्। "तव करुणा असीमा, राजन्!" इति वदन्तौ तौ शिबिं आशिषा अशाश्वतकीर्तिं प्रदत्तवन्तौ। शिबेः कथा शाश्वतं स्मरणीया अभवत् यत् सत्यकरुणा आत्मत्यागं अपेक्षते इति।

description: When righteous anger rises against injustice
contentEnglish:
Parashurama, the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu, was born to the sage Jamadagni and Renuka. Though a Brahmin by birth, he was also a formidable warrior, trained by Lord Shiva himself. He lived peacefully in his father's ashram, embodying both spiritual wisdom and martial prowess.

The peace was shattered when King Kartavirya Arjuna, drunk with power and his thousand arms, visited the ashram. The sage welcomed him with humble hospitality, serving a feast that appeared miraculously through the sacred wish-fulfilling cow, Kamadhenu. The greedy king, coveting this divine cow, forcibly took her away despite the sage's protests.

When Parashurama returned and learned of this outrage, a righteous fury awakened within him. This was not mere anger, but the wrath of dharma itself against adharma. His eyes blazed like molten fire as he gripped his axe, the divine weapon gifted by Shiva. The very earth trembled at the intensity of his resolve.

Parashurama stormed the royal palace, his form radiating terrible power. King Kartavirya's thousand arms proved worthless before this force of divine justice. In a fierce battle that shook the heavens, Parashurama's axe severed all thousand arms before striking down the tyrant king. He reclaimed Kamadhenu and restored her to the ashram.

But fate had more tragedy in store. The king's sons, seeking revenge, attacked the ashram when Parashurama was away and murdered the defenseless sage Jamadagni. When Parashurama discovered his father's blood staining the sacred ground, his grief transformed into a terrible vow.

Twenty-one times he circled the earth, his axe dripping with the blood of corrupt warriors who had abandoned dharma for tyranny. His wrath was not born of personal vendetta but of a fierce commitment to justice. Through his terrifying campaign, Parashurama demonstrated that when righteousness is trampled, divine anger rises to restore cosmic balance, reminding all that power without dharma invites its own destruction.
contentSanskrit:
परशुरामः विष्णोः षष्ठः अवतारः आसीत्। सः जमदग्निऋषेः रेणुकायाश्च पुत्रः आसीत्। यद्यपि ब्राह्मणः आसीत्, तथापि शिवेन प्रशिक्षितः महान् योद्धा आसीत्।

एकदा कार्तवीर्यार्जुनः नाम सहस्रबाहुः राजा आश्रमं प्राप्तवान्। ऋषिः तं सत्कारेण स्वागतवान्। कामधेनुः नाम दिव्यगौः आश्चर्यजनकं भोजनं प्रदत्तवती। लोभी राजा तां गां बलात् नीतवान्।

परशुरामः आगत्य एतत् अधर्मं श्रुत्वा क्रोधेन ज्वलितः अभवत्। सः परशुं गृहीत्वा राजभवनं प्रति गतवान्। तस्य नेत्रे अग्निवत् प्रज्वलिते। पृथिवी कम्पिता अभवत्।

भीषणे युद्धे परशुरामः राज्ञः सर्वाणि सहस्रबाहून् छित्त्वा तं हतवान्। कामधेनुं पुनः आश्रमं नीतवान्। परन्तु राज्ञः पुत्राः प्रतिशोधार्थं जमदग्निं हतवन्तः।

पितुः रक्तं दृष्ट्वा परशुरामः भयङ्करं प्रतिज्ञां कृतवान्। एकविंशतिवारं पृथिवीं परिक्रम्य दुष्टक्षत्रियान् संहृतवान्। तस्य क्रोधः व्यक्तिगता न आसीत्, अपितु धर्मस्य रक्षणार्थं आसीत्।

परशुरामः प्रमाणं कृतवान् यत् धर्मस्य रक्षणार्थं दिव्यक्रोधः आवश्यकः भवति। शक्तिः विना धर्मं विनाशं आह्वयति इति सत्यम्।

description: Unmatched bravery in the face of impossible odds
contentEnglish:
On the thirteenth day of the Kurukshetra war, the Kauravas devised their most deadly stratagem—the Chakravyuha, a spinning wheel formation so complex that only a handful of warriors knew how to penetrate and exit it. When Dronacharya arranged this impenetrable maze, the Pandavas faced their darkest hour, for Arjuna, who knew the secret, was lured away from the battlefield.

Young Abhimanyu, son of Arjuna and Subhadra, stepped forward with fearless determination. Though only sixteen years old, his eyes blazed with the fire of a true warrior. "I know how to enter the Chakravyuha," he declared. "I learned it in my mother's womb when father explained it to mother. Though I do not know the way out, my courage will forge the path!"

Despite the protests of his elders and the tears of his young wife Uttara, Abhimanyu charged into the deadly formation like a lion entering a den of wolves. His chariot wheels thundered across the battlefield as he shattered the first six layers of the formation with breathtaking skill. Arrows flew from his bow like lightning bolts, and seasoned warriors fell before his unprecedented valor.

Inside the Chakravyuha, Abhimanyu fought like a tornado of divine fury. Alone against thousands, he battled seven maharathis simultaneously—warriors who were each capable of defeating thousands. His sword danced, his arrows sang, and his courage burned brighter than the midday sun. Even his enemies were awestruck by such magnificent bravery.

When his chariot was destroyed, he fought on foot. When his sword shattered, he wielded a chariot wheel as his weapon. When his weapons were broken and he stood exhausted and wounded, surrounded by cowards who attacked him together in violation of all dharma, Abhimanyu faced them with unwavering dignity. With his last breath, he struck down his assailants, falling like a great tree in the forest.

Though Abhimanyu could not exit the maze, his sacrifice became immortal. He proved that true heroism lies not in survival but in facing impossible odds with unshakeable courage. His valor that day became the benchmark for bravery—a sixteen-year-old warrior whose courage made the gods weep and whose name became synonymous with fearless heroism for all eternity.
contentSanskrit:
कुरुक्षेत्रयुद्धस्य त्रयोदशे दिने कौरवैः चक्रव्यूहः निर्मितः आसीत्। द्रोणाचार्येण निर्मितं एतत् दुर्भेद्यं व्यूहं केवलं कतिपयाः योद्धाराः एव भेत्तुं निर्गन्तुं च जानन्ति स्म।

अर्जुनः युद्धभूम्याः दूरं नीतः आसीत्। तदा युवा अभिमन्युः निर्भयतया अग्रे आगतवान्। यद्यपि सः केवलं षोडशवर्षीयः आसीत्, तथापि सत्यवीरः आसीत्। "अहं चक्रव्यूहं प्रवेष्टुं जानामि," इति अवदत्। "मातुः गर्भे पितुः उपदेशं श्रुतवान् अस्मि। निर्गमनं न जानामि, परन्तु मम साहसं मार्गं निर्मास्यति!"

ज्येष्ठानां निषेधं उत्तरायाः अश्रूणि च उपेक्ष्य अभिमन्युः सिंहवत् व्यूहं प्राविशत्। प्रथमाः षट् स्तराः अद्भुतकौशलेन भित्त्वा सः अग्रे गतवान्। तस्य बाणाः विद्युत्वत् शत्रून् पातयन्ति स्म।

चक्रव्यूहे अभिमन्युः एकः सहस्रैः सह युयुधे। सप्तमहारथिभिः सह एकसमये युद्धं कृतवान्। तस्य साहसं मध्याह्नसूर्यवत् प्रज्वलितम्। शत्रवः अपि तस्य वीरतां प्रशंसन्ति स्म।

यदा तस्य रथः नष्टः अभवत्, पदातिः युयुधे। यदा खड्गः भग्नः अभवत्, रथचक्रं शस्त्रवत् प्रयुक्तवान्। अन्ते क्लान्तः घायलः च आसीत्, परन्तु तस्य साहसं न न्यूनम् अभवत्।

अधर्मेण पराजितः अभिमन्युः, परन्तु तस्य वीरता अमरा अभवत्। सः प्रमाणं कृतवान् यत् सत्यवीरता जीवने नास्ति, अपितु असम्भवं साहसेन सामना कर्तुं भवति। षोडशवर्षीयस्य वीरस्य नाम शाश्वतं अभवत्।

description: A divine manifestation that strikes fear in the hearts of evil
contentEnglish:
The demon king Hiranyakashipu ruled with absolute tyranny, his heart consumed by hatred for Lord Vishnu. Through severe penances, he had obtained a boon that made him virtually invincible—he could not be killed by man or beast, neither inside nor outside, not during day nor night, not on earth nor in sky, and by no weapon created.

Drunk with this power, he declared himself god and demanded that all worship him alone. But his own son, the devoted Prahlada, refused to abandon his faith in Vishnu, singing the Lord's praises despite horrific tortures. The demon's rage knew no bounds. When Prahlada claimed Vishnu existed everywhere, Hiranyakashipu kicked a pillar in his palace, roaring, "If your god is everywhere, let him emerge from this pillar!"

The pillar exploded with a sound that shook the three worlds. From within emerged a form so terrifying that even the bravest warriors trembled. It was neither fully man nor fully lion, but a horrifying amalgamation—Narasimha. His mane blazed like wildfire, his eyes burned red as molten copper, and his fangs dripped with divine fury. His roar split the heavens and made the earth quake.

Hiranyakashipu, who had never known fear, felt terror grip his heart for the first time. He unleashed all his weapons, but they shattered against the divine form. Narasimha's laugh was more terrifying than his roar—a sound that echoed the approaching doom of evil itself. With movements swift as lightning, the Lord seized the demon king.

At twilight—neither day nor night—at the threshold—neither inside nor outside—Narasimha placed the demon on his lap—neither earth nor sky—and with his razor-sharp claws—no weapon—tore open the tyrant's chest. The demon's screams of terror filled all the worlds as divine justice was delivered. His intestines were draped around Narasimha's neck like a victory garland, a sight so fearsome that even the gods dared not approach.

The Lord's terrible form continued to rage, his fury unabated. Only when young Prahlada approached with innocent devotion did the wrathful eyes soften. The terrifying Narasimha transformed into a loving protector for his devotee, proving that the divine assumes the most fearsome form to destroy evil, ensuring that righteousness prevails and the wicked tremble before cosmic justice.
contentSanskrit:
हिरण्यकशिपुः राक्षसराजः विष्णुद्वेषेन पूर्णः आसीत्। कठोरतपसा वरं प्राप्तवान् - न नरेण न पशुना, न अन्तः न बहिः, न दिवा न रात्रौ, न भूमौ न आकाशे, न केनापि अस्त्रेण मरणं भविष्यति इति।

शक्त्या मत्तः सः स्वयमेव देवः इति घोषयामास। सर्वान् स्वं पूजयितुम् आदिशत्। परन्तु तस्य पुत्रः प्रह्लादः विष्णुं भक्त्या पूजयति स्म। राक्षसस्य क्रोधः असीमः अभवत्। यदा प्रह्लादः अवदत् "विष्णुः सर्वत्र अस्ति," तदा हिरण्यकशिपुः स्तम्भं प्रहृत्य गर्जितवान् - "यदि तव देवः सर्वत्र अस्ति, तर्हि अस्मात् स्तम्भात् बहिः आगच्छतु!"

स्तम्भः विस्फोटितः। ततः भयानकं रूपं प्रादुर्भूतम् - नरसिंहः। न पूर्णमनुष्यः न पूर्णसिंहः, अपितु भीषणं मिश्रणम्। तस्य अयालः अग्निवत् ज्वलति स्म, नेत्रे रक्तवर्णे, दंष्ट्राः भयानकाः। तस्य गर्जनं स्वर्गं भूमिं च कम्पयामास।

हिरण्यकशिपुः प्रथमवारं भयं अनुभूतवान्। सः सर्वास्त्राणि प्रयुक्तवान्, परन्तु ते भग्नाः अभवन्। नरसिंहस्य हास्यं गर्जनात् अपि भयानकम् आसीत्।

संध्यासमये—न दिवा न रात्रौ—देहल्यां—न अन्तः न बहिः—नरसिंहः राक्षसं स्वोरौ स्थापयामास—न भूमौ न आकाशे—नखैः—न अस्त्रेण—तस्य वक्षः विदार्य हतवान्। राक्षसस्य भयकरुणाध्वनयः सर्वान् लोकान् पूरयामासुः।

नरसिंहस्य भयानकरूपं क्रोधेन ज्वलितम्। केवलं युवप्रह्लादः भक्त्या आगच्छत्, तदा क्रुद्धनेत्रे कोमले अभवताम्। नरसिंहः भक्तस्य रक्षकः अभवत्, प्रमाणं कृत्वा यत् दिव्यं अधर्मविनाशाय भयानकरूपं धारयति।

description: The consequences of greed and unrighteous actions
contentEnglish:
After eighteen days of bloody warfare, the Kurukshetra battlefield lay covered with the corpses of millions. The stench of death hung heavy in the air, and vultures circled endlessly overhead. Duryodhana, the architect of this catastrophic war, found himself alone—all his brothers dead, his army decimated, and his ambitions reduced to ashes.

Wounded and desperate, he hid in a lake, using his mystic powers to create a watery shelter. But the Pandavas discovered his cowardly refuge. "Come out and face us!" they called. "You who dragged the world into war, who humiliated Draupadi in the assembly, who poisoned your cousins and burned them alive in a house of lac—show yourself!"

Forced out by taunts and dharma, Duryodhana agreed to a final mace duel with Bhima. As they circled each other, the extent of Duryodhana's moral degradation became apparent. This was the man who had cheated in dice, who had attempted to molest Draupadi publicly, who had laughed at the blind king Dhritarashtra's inability to see his sons' corruption. Every evil deed seemed to emanate from his very being.

The fight was brutal. Bhima, remembering Draupadi's vow that she would not tie her hair until it was washed in Dushasana's blood, remembered the oath that he would break Duryodhana's thigh—the very thigh the villain had obscenely slapped in Draupadi's presence. With a mighty blow that violated the rules of mace combat, Bhima shattered both of Duryodhana's thighs.

Duryodhana lay in the dust and blood, his body broken, still spewing venom from his mouth. Even in defeat, he showed no remorse, no recognition of his heinous crimes. He cursed the Pandavas, blamed everyone but himself, his words as repulsive as the corruption that had consumed his soul. The sight of him wallowing in his own blood and bile was deeply disgusting—a once-mighty prince reduced to a pathetic, unrepentant wretch.

As Ashwatthama approached to hear his king's dying words, Duryodhana's final command revealed the depths of his depravity—he ordered the massacre of the sleeping Pandava camp, a plan so vile and cowardly that even his loyal friend hesitated. The story of Duryodhana's end serves as a revolting reminder of how unchecked greed, pride, and wickedness can reduce a human being to something utterly contemptible, deserving only of disgust and aversion.
contentSanskrit:
अष्टादशदिवसीययुद्धस्य अन्ते कुरुक्षेत्रं शवैः पूर्णम् आसीत्। मृत्युगन्धः सर्वत्र आसीत्। दुर्योधनः, युद्धस्य कर्ता, एकाकी आसीत्—सर्वे भ्रातरः हताः, सेना विनष्टा।

घायलः भीतः च सः सरसि अलुभत्। मायया जलीयं आश्रयं निर्मितवान्। परन्तु पाण्डवाः तं प्राप्नुवन्। "बहिः आगच्छ युद्धं कुरु!" इति अवदन्। "त्वं यः द्रौपदीं सभायां अपमानितवान्, यः विषेण भ्रातॄन् मारयितुं प्रयतवान्—दर्शनं देहि!"

दुर्योधनः भीमेन सह गदायुद्धं कृतवान्। तस्य अधर्मः स्पष्टः आसीत्। भीमः द्रौपद्याः अपमानस्य स्मारणं कृत्वा दुर्योधनस्य ऊरू भग्नवान्।

दुर्योधनः रक्तो धूलिधूसरितः पतितः। पराजये अपि सः पश्चात्तापं न कृतवान्, अपितु पाण्डवान् निन्दितवान्। तस्य स्थितिः बीभत्सा आसीत्।

अश्वत्थामा यदा समीपम् आगतः, दुर्योधनः सुप्तपाण्डवानां शिबिरे हत्यां कर्तुं आदिष्टवान्। एषा योजना एतावती नीचा आसीत् यत् तस्य मित्रमपि संकोचम् अनुभवत्। दुर्योधनस्य अन्तः स्मारयति यत् अधर्मः, लोभः, गर्वः च मनुष्यं कथमधमं, घृणितं च करोति। बीभत्सस्य पराकाष्ठा एषा।

description: The cosmic form that reveals the infinite universe
contentEnglish:
On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, faced with the prospect of fighting his own kin, Arjuna was overcome with doubt and despair. To remove his delusion and reveal the ultimate truth of existence, Lord Krishna granted him divine vision and revealed his cosmic form—the Vishwarupa.

What Arjuna saw defied all description and imagination. He saw the entire universe contained within the Lord's body. Countless suns and moons blazed together with the radiance of a thousand suns rising at once. He saw all beings, all gods, all sages, and all creatures, moving and unmoving, existing simultaneously within the Divine.

Every form of existence was there—the gentle and the terrible, the creator and the destroyer. He saw the sons of Dhritarashtra rushing into the Lord's fearful mouths like moths into a fire, consumed by Time itself. The boundaries of space and time dissolved, revealing the Lord as the beginning, middle, and end of all things.

Trembling with awe and amazement, Arjuna bowed his head. "I see You without beginning, middle, or end," he cried. "Your eyes are the sun and moon, and your face blazes like fire, warming the entire universe." The sight was so overwhelming—so "Adbhuta" (wondrous)—that Arjuna could barely sustain it.

This divine revelation taught humanity that the seen world is but a fragment of reality. Behind every finite form lies the Infinite. The Vishwarupa demonstrated that God is not just a ruler of the world but the very substance of it, inspiring a sense of wonder that transcends fear and leads to absolute surrender.
contentSanskrit:
कुरुक्षेत्रस्य युद्धभूमौ, स्वजनान् दृष्ट्वा अर्जुनः विषादग्रस्तः अभवत्। तस्य मोहं दूरीकर्तुं श्रीकृष्णः तस्मै दिव्यदृष्टिं दत्त्वा स्वस्य विश्वरूपं दर्शितवान्।

यत् अर्जुनेन दृष्टं, तत् अवर्णनीयम् आसीत्। सः भगवति सम्पूर्णं ब्रह्माण्डं अपश्यत्। अनेकसूर्याणां कान्तिः एकत्र उदिता इव आसीत्। सर्वे देवाः, ऋषयः, चराचरजीवाः तत्र आसन्।

तत्र शान्तं उग्रं च रूपं आसीत्। धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः अग्निमिव तस्य मुखे प्रविशन्ति स्म। दिक्कालादीनां सीमाः समाप्ताः अभवन्। भगवान् एव आदिः, मध्यः, अन्तः च आसीत्।

विस्मयेन कम्पितः अर्जुनः नतमस्तकः अभवत्। "अहं त्वां आदिमध्यान्तशून्यं पश्यामि," इति सः अवदत्। एतत् दृश्यं अत्यन्तं अद्भुतं आसीत् यत् अर्जुनः सोढुं न अशक्नोत्।

एतत् विश्वरूपं दर्शयति यत् दृश्यमानं जगत् सत्यस्य एकः अंशः एव। प्रत्येकस्य रूपस्य पृष्ठतः अनन्तः अस्ति। ईश्वरेण विना किमपि नास्ति इति ज्ञात्वा अर्जुनः शरणागतः अभवत्।

storyTitle: Buddha's Enlightenment Under the Bodhi Tree
storyTitleSanskrit: बुद्ध का बोधि वृक्ष के नीचे ज्ञान
description: The serene journey to ultimate peace and enlightenment
contentEnglish:
Born as Prince Siddhartha, he lived a life of supreme luxury, shielded from all suffering. But when he witnessed the four sights—an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and an ascetic—he realized that life is full of suffering (Dukkha). Determined to find the path to peace, he renounced his kingdom, his wealth, and his family, stepping into the unknown.

For years he practiced severe austerities, starving himself until he was skeletal, but found no peace. Realizing that neither extreme indulgence nor extreme asceticism was the answer, he chose the "Middle Way." He sat beneath a Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, resolving not to rise until he had found the ultimate truth.

Mara, the demon of illusion, tried to disturb him with storms, armies of demons, and temptations of pleasure. But Siddhartha remained unmoved, his mind as still as a mountain lake. He touched the earth to witness his unwavering resolve. One by one, the layers of ignorance peeled away.

As the morning star rose, he attained Enlightenment. He understood the cause of suffering—desire and ignorance—and the way to end it. He became the Buddha, the "Awakened One." A profound peace, the Shanta Rasa, radiated from him, calming even the wild animals of the forest.

His face shone with the tranquility of Nirvana—a peace that is not merely the absence of conflict, but a state of perfect inner stillness and compassion. He spent the rest of his life sharing this path of peace, teaching that the greatest victory is the conquest of one's own mind.
contentSanskrit:
राजकुमारः सिद्धार्थः सुखे पालितः आसीत्। परन्तु यदा सः वृद्धं, रुग्णं, मृतं, सन्यासिं च अपश्यत्, तदा सः ज्ञातवान् यत् संसारः दुःखमयः अस्ति। शान्तिं अन्वेष्टुं सः राज्यं, धनं, परिवारं च त्यक्तवान्।

वर्षाणि यावत् सः कठोरतपः कृतवान्, परन्तु शान्तिं न प्राप्तवान्। तदा सः मध्यममार्गं स्वीकृत्य बोधिवृक्षस्य अधः उपविष्टवान्। "सत्यं अप्राप्य न उत्तिष्ठामि" इति प्रतिज्ञां कृतवान्।

मारः तं विचलितुं प्रयतवान्, परन्तु सिद्धार्थः अचलः अतिष्ठत्। तस्य मनः शान्तसरोवरवत् आसीत्। अज्ञानस्य अन्धकारः नष्टः अभवत्।

प्रातःकाले सः बुद्धत्वं प्राप्तवान्। सः दुःखस्य कारणं निवारणं च ज्ञातवान्। सः 'बुद्धः' अभवत्। तस्मात् अपूर्वा शान्तिः (शान्तरसः) प्रसृता।

तस्य मुखे निर्वाणस्य शान्तिः आसीत्। एषा शान्तिः केवलं युद्धस्य अभावः न, अपितु मनसः पूर्णस्थिरता अस्ति। सः जीवनपर्यन्तं एं शान्तिमार्गं पाठितवान् - "मनसः विजयः एव महान् विजयः।"
